Ἰησοῦς.long: Jesus; the Greek form of Joshua; Jesus, son of Eliezer; Jesus, surnamed Justus.
Ἰησοῦς.sd: Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord and two (three) other Israelites
Ἰησοῦς.as:
Ἰησοῦς, -οῦ, dat., voc. -οῦ, acc., -οῦν (Heb. יְהוֹשׁוּעַ, יְהֹשֻׁעַ, יֵשׁוּעַ),
1.JESUS: Mt 1:21, al.; ὁ Ἰ, Mt 3:13, al.; Ἰ. Χριστός, Mt 1:1, Mk 1:1, al.; Χρ. Ἰ., Ro 2:26, al.; κύριος Ἰ., Ac 28:31, al.; Ἰησοῦ, voc., Mk 1:24, al.
2.Joshua: Ac 7:45, He 4:8.
3.Jesus, son of Eliezer: Lk 3:29.
4.Jesus, surnamed Justus: Col 4:11.
5. v.s. βαραββᾶς.

Ἰσαάκ.sd: Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of Abraham
Ἰσαάκ.as:
Ἰσαάκ
(in MSS. sometimes -σάκ; cf. Deiss., BS, 189; Thack., Gr., 100), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἴσακος, -ου), (Heb. יִצְחָק),
Isaac (Ge 17:19, al.): Mt 1:2, Ro 9:10, al.

Ἰακώβ.long: (Hebrew), Jacob, (a) the patriarch, son of Isaac, (b) father of Joseph, the husband of Mary.
Ἰακώβ.sd: Jacob (i.e. Ja`akob), the progenitor of the Israelites
Ἰακώβ.as:
Ἰακώβ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. יַעֲקֹב),
Jacob;
1. The patriarch: Mt 1:28:11, Jo 4:5, 6, Ac 7:8, al,; as in Heb. (cf. Nu 23:7, Is 41:8, Si 23:12, al.), of his descendants, Ro 11:26(LXX).
2. The father-in-law of Mary: Mt 1:15, 16 (on the form as distinct from that of the next word, v. Deiss., BS, 3161)

Ἰούδας.sd: Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its region
Ἰούδας.as:
Ἰούδας, -α, dat. -ᾳ, acc. -αν
(so in LXX, and also rarely, Ἰουδά, indecl.; cf. Thack., Gr., 163), (Heb. יְהוּדָה);
1.Judah, son of Jacob: Mt 1:2, 3, Lk 3:33; φυλή Ἰ., Re 5:57:5; by meton., of the tribe, He 7:14; of its confines, γῆ Ἰ., Mt 2:6;πόλις Ἰ., Lk 1:39.
2.Judah (unknown): Lk 3:30.
3.Judas Iscariot (v.s. Ἰσκαριώτης): Mt 10:4, Mk 3:19, Lk 6:16, Jo 6:7113:2, al.
4.Judas, the Lord's brother (v.s. ἀδελφός): Mt 13:55, Mk 6:3 (prob.), Ju 1.
5.Judas the Apostle, son of James (v.s. Θαδδαῖος): Lk 6:16, Jo 14:22, Ac 1:13.
6.Judas, of Damascus: Ac 9:11.
7.Judas, surnamed Βαρσαββᾶς (q.v.): Ac 15:22, 27, 32.
8.Judas the Galilean: Ac 5:37.

Ἰωβήδ.as:
Ἰωβήδ (WH, -βήλ, Lk 3:32; Rec., RV, Ὠβήδ), ὁ, indecl.,
Jobed (Obed): Mt 1:5, Lk 3:32.†

Ἰεσσαί.long: (Hebrew), Jesse, son of Obed, and father of King David.
Ἰεσσαί.as:
Ἰεσσαί (FlJ, -σσαῖος), ὁ (Heb. יִשַׁי, Ru 4:17, al.),
Jesse: Mt 1:5, 6, Lk 3:32, Ac 13:22(LXX), Ro 15:12(LXX).†

Ἰωσαφάτ.long: (Hebrew), Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, son of Asaph, father of Joram, an ancestor of Jesus.

Ἰωράμ.long: (Hebrew), Joram, Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat and father of Uzziah.

Ἰωαθάμ.long: Jotham, son of Uzziah and father of Ahaz.
Ἰωαθάμ.as:
Ἰωάθαμ (WH, -θάμ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. יוֹתָם),
Jotham, King of Judah: Mt 1:9.†

Ἰεχονίας.long: (Hebrew), Jechoniah, son of Josiah and father of Salathiel.
Ἰεχονίας.as:
Ἰεχονίας, -ον, ὁ (Heb. יְהוֹיָכִין, Jehoiakin),
Jechoniah: Mt 1:11, 12.†

Ἰωσήφ.sd: Joseph, the name of seven Israelites
Ἰωσήφ.as:
Ἰωσήφ, indecl.
(FlJ, Ἰώσηπος, -ου), ὁ (Heb. יוֹסֵף),
Joseph;
1. the Son of Jacob: Jo 4:5, Ac 7:9, 13, 14, 18, He 11:21, 22, Re 7:8.
2. In the genealogy of our Lord,
(a) the son of Matthias: Lk 3:24;
(b) the son Joram: Lk 3:30.
3. The husband of Mary, the Lord's mother: Mt 1:16 ff., Lk 1:27, Jo 1:46, al.
4. One of the brethren of our Lord (v.s. ἀδελφός): Mt 13:55.
5. Son of Mary: Mt 27:56 (-σῆς, WH, mg., RV).
6.Joseph of Arimatbæa: Mt 27:57, 59, Mk 15:43, 45, Lk 23:50, Jo 19:38.
7. v.s. Βαρνάβας.
8. v.s. Βαρσαβᾶς.

ἰδού.der: second person singular imperative middle voice of G1492 (εἴδω);
ἰδού.as:
ἰδού,
[in LXX chiefly for הִנֵּה,]
prop. imperat. 2 aor. mid. of ὁράω, used as a demonstrative particle, with frequency much greater in LXX and NT than in cl. (v. M, Pr., 11),
lo, behold, see: Mt 10:1611:813:3, Mk 3:32, Lk 2:48, I Co 15:51, Ja 5:9, Ju 14, Re 1:7, al.; after gen. absol., Mt 1:202:1, 1312:46, al.; καὶ ἰδού, Mt 2:9 (and freq.), Lk 1:2010:25, Ac 12:7, al.; in elliptical sentences, taking the place of copula or predicate (like הִנֵּה in Heb.), Mt 3:17, Lk 5:1222:31, 47, Ac 8:27, 36 al.

ἵνα.sd: compare G3588 (ὁ)); in order that (denoting the purpose or the result)
ἵνα.kj: albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as, (so) that, (for) to
ἵνα.der: probably from the same as the former part of G1438 (ἑαυτοῦ) (through the demonstrative idea;
ἵνα.as:
ἵνα,
I.adverb (poët., Hom., al.),
1. of place, where, whither.
2. of circumstance, when.
II.Conjunction,
1. prop., final, denoting purpose or end (cl.), that, in order that, usually the first word in the clause, but sometimes (cl. also) preceded by an emphatic word (Ac 19:4, Ro 11:31 (?), Ga 2:10, al.);
(a) c. optat. (so in cl. after historic tenses): after a pres., Eph 1:17 (but WH, mg., subjc.; v. Burton, § 225, Rem., 2);
(b) c. subjc.: after a pres., Mk 4:21, Lk 6:34, Jo 3:15, Ac 2:25, Ro 1:11, al.; after a pf., Mt 1:22, Jo 5:23, I Co 9:22, al.; after an imperat. (pres. or aor.), Mt 7:1, Mk 11:25, Jo 10:38, I Co 7:5, al.; after a delib. subjc., Mk 1:38, al.; after a fut., Lk 16:4, Jo 14:3, I Co 15:28, al.; after historic tenses (where optat. in cl.; WM, 359 f.; M, Pr., 196 f.), Mk 6:41 (impf.), Jo 4:8 (plpf.), Mk 3:14 (aor.), al.;
(c) in late writers (M, Pr., 35; Burton, §§ 198, 199), c. indic. fut: Lk 20:10, I Pe 3:1, al.;
(d) as often in eccl. writers (Thayer, s.v.), c. indic. pres.: I Co 4:6, Ga 4:17, al. (?; but v. Burton, § 198, Rem.);
(e)εἰς (διὰ) τοῦτο, ἵνα: Jo 18:37, I Ti 1:16, al.; τούτου χάριν, Tit 1:5;
(f) elliptical constructions: omission of the principal verb, Jo 1:8, II Th 3:9, I Jo 2:19, al.; of the final verb, Ro 4:16, II Co 8:13, al.
2. In late writers, definitive, = inf. (WM, 420; Bl., § 69, 1), that;
(a) after verbs of wishing, caring, striving, etc.: θέλω, Mt 7:12, al.; ζητῶ, I Co 4:214:12; ζηλόω, I Co 14:1, al.;
(b) after verbs of saying, asking, exhorting: εἰπεῖν, Mt 4:3, al.; ἐρωτῶ, Mk 7:26, al.; παρακαλῶ, Mt 14:36, I Co 1:10, al., etc.;
(c) after words expressing expediency, etc.: συμφέρει, Mt 18:6, Jo 11:50, al.; ἱκανός, Mt 8:8, Lk 7:6; χρείαν ἔχω, Jo 2:25, al, etc.;
(d) after substantives, adding further definition: ὥρα, Jo 12:2313:1; χρόνος, Re 2:21; συνήθεια, Jo 18:39; μισθός, I Co 9:18.
3. In late writers, ecbatic, denoting the result, = ὥστε, that, so that (M, Pr., 206 ff.; WM, 572; Bl., § 69, 3; Burton, § 223): Ro 11:11, I Co 7:29, I Th 5:4, al. (but v. Thayer, s.v.); so with the formula referring to the fulfilment of prophecy, ἵνα πληρωθῇ, Mt 1:222:144:14, Jo 13:18, al.

Ἰουδαία.long: Judea, a Roman province, capital Jerusalem.
Ἰουδαία.sd: the Judæan land (i.e. Judæa), a region of Palestine

Ἱεροσόλυμα.long: the Greek form of the Hebrew name: Jerusalem.
Ἱεροσόλυμα.sd: Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim), the capitol of Palestine
Ἱεροσόλυμα.as:
Ἱεροσόλυμα (WH, Ἰερ-, v. Intr., § 408), -ων, τά (on πᾶσα Ἱ., Mt 2:3, v. WM, 794; M, Pr., 48, 244; Thayer, s.v.), and Ἱερουσαλήμ (WH, Ἰερ-), ἡ., indecl., as always in LXX exc. some parts of Apocr. (Heb. יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, יְרוּשָׁלֵם), the former always in FlJ, Mk, Jo ev. and Mt (exc. Mt 27:37), and most freq. in Lk, the latter always in He, Re, and by St. Paul (exc. Ga 1:17, 182:1),
Jerusalem: Mt 2:1, Mk 3:8, Jo 1:19, al.; its inhabitants, Mt 2:33:523:37, Lk 13:34. Symbolically, ἡ- ἄνω Ἱ., Ga 4:26, contrasted with ἡ νῦν Ἱ., Ga 4:25; Ἱ. ἐπουράνιος, He 12:22; ἡ καινὴ Ἱ., Re 3:1221:2, 10.

Ἰουδαῖος.der: from G2448 (Ἰουδά) (in the sense of G2455 (Ἰούδας) as a country);
Ἰουδαῖος.as:
Ἰουδαῖος, -αία, -αῖον
(< Ἰούδας),
Jewish: ἀνήρ, Ac 10:2822:3; ἄνθρωπος, Ac 21:39; ψευδοπροφήτης, 13:6; ἀσχιερεύς, 19:14; γυνή, 16:124:24; γῆ, Jo 3:22; χώρα, Mk 1:5. Substantively,
(a)Ἰουδαῖος, ὁ, a Jew: Jo 4:9, Ac 18:24, Ro 2:28; pl., Re 2:93:9; οἱ Ἰ., Mt 2:2, Mk 7:3, Jo 2:6, al.; Ἰ. τε καὶ Ἕλληνες, Ac 14:1, al.; κ. προσήλυτοι, Ac 2:10; ἔθνη τε κ. Ἰ., Ac 14:5; οἱ κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη Ἰ., Ac 21:21; of Jewish Christians, Ga 2:13; of the ruling class who opposed Jesus, Jo 1:192:185:1011:813:33, al.;
(b)Ἰουδαία, -ας, ἡ (sc. γῆ, χώρα, cf. Jo 3:22, Mk 1:5), (Heb. יְהוּדָה), Judæa: Mt 2:1, Lk 1:5, Jo 4:3, al.

Ἰσραήλ.long: (Hebrew), Israel, surname of Jacob, then the Jewish people, the people of God.
Ἰσραήλ.sd: Israel (i.e. Jisrael), the adopted name of Jacob, including his descendants (literally or figuratively)
Ἰσραήλ.as:
Ἰσραήλ (FlJ, Ἰσράηλος, -ου), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. יִשְׂרָאֵל, Ge 32:28),
Israel: ὁ οἶκος Ἰ., Ac 7:42(LXX), al.; λαός, Ac 4:10; υἱοί, Ac 5:21, al.; αἱ φυλαὶ τοῦ Ἰ., Mt 19:28, al. By meton., for the Israelites, Mt 2:6, Lk 1:54, Ro 11:2, al.; ὁ λαὸς Ἰ., Ac 4:10; γῆ Ἰ., Mt 2:20, 21; βασιλεὺς Ἰ., Mt 27:42, Jo 1:50; ἡ ἐλπὶς τοῦ Ἰ., Ac 28:20; ὁ Ἰ. τοῦ θεοῦ (of Christians), Ga 6:16; ὁ Ἰ. κατὰ σάρκα, I Co 10:18.

ἵστημι.long: trans: (a) I make to stand, place, set up, establish, appoint; mid: I place myself, stand, (b) I set in balance, weigh; intrans: (c) I stand, stand by, stand still; met: I stand ready, stand firm, am steadfast.
ἵστημι.sd: to stand (transitively or intransitively), used in various applications (literally or figuratively)
ἵστημι.kj: abide, appoint, bring, continue, covenant, establish, hold up, lay, present, set (up), stanch, stand (by, forth, still, up)
ἵστημι.der: a prolonged form of a primary (of the same meaning, and used for it in certain tenses);
ἵστημι.as:
ἵστημι, and in late writers, also ἱστάνω (Veitch, s.v.; Bl., § 23, 2; M, Pr., 55),
[in LXX chiefly for עמד, קוּם, also for נצב ni., hi., יצב hith., etc.].
I. Trans, in pres., impf., fut. and 1 aor. act. and in the tenses of the pass.
1.to make to stand, to place, set, set up, establish, appoint: c. acc. pers., Mk 7:9, Ac 1:236:1317:31, He 10:9; id. seq. ἐπί, c. acc. loc., Mt 4:5, Lk 4:9; ἐν μέσῳ, Mt 18:2, Mk 9:36, Jo 8:[3]; ἐνώπιον, Ac 6:6; παρ’ ἑαυτῷ, Lk 9:47; ἐκ δεξιῶν, Mt 25:33; mid., to place oneself, to stand: Re 18:15; so also pass., to be made to stand, to stand: Mt 2:9, Lk 11:1819:8, II Co 13:1, al.
2.to set in a balance, to weigh (cl.; LXX for שׁקל, Is 46:6, al.): Mt 26:15.
II. Intrans., in pf., plpf. (with sense of pres. and impf.; M, Pr., 147 f.) and 2 aor. act., to stand, stand by, stand still: Mt 20:3226:73, Mk 10:49, Lk 8:44, Jo 1:353:29, Ac 16:9, al.; seq. ἐν, Mt 6:5, al.; ἐνώπιον, Ac 10:30, al.; πρός, c. dat. loc., Jo 18:16; ἐπί, c. gen. loc., Lk 6:17, Ac 5:2325:10, al.; ἔμπροσθεν, Mt 27:11; κύκλῳ, Re 7:11; ἐκ δεξιῶν, Lk 1:11; ἐπί, c. acc., Mt 13:2, Re 3:20; παρά, Lk 5:2; ἐκεῖ, Mk 11:5; ὧδε, Mk 9:1; ὅπου, Mk 13:14; ἔξω, Mt 12:46; μακρόθεν, Lk 18:13; πόρρωθεν, Lk 17:12. Metaph., to stand ready, stand firm, be steadfast: I Co 7:3710:12, Eph 6:11, 13, 14, Col 4:12; τ. πίστει, Ro 11:20; ἐν τ. ἀληθείᾳ, Jo 8:44; ἐν τ. χάριτι, Ro 5:2; ἐν τ. εὐαγγελίῳ, I Co 15:1 (cf. ἀν-, ἐπ-ἀν-, ἐξ-ἀν, ἀνθ-, ἀφ-, δι-, ἐν-, ἐξ-, ἐπ- (-μαι), ἐφ-, κατ-εφ-, συν-εφ-, καθ-, ἀντι-καθ-, ἀπο-καθ-, μεθ-, παρ-, περι-, προ-, συν-ίστημι).

Ἰερεμίας.as:
Ἰερεμίας (T, Rec. Ἱερ-; v. WH, § 408), -ου, ὁ (Heb. יִרְמְיָה, יִרְמְיָהוּ),
Jeremiah the prophet: Mt 2:1716:1427:9 (a ref. to Za 11:13).†

Ἰωάννης.long: John: the Baptist, the apostle, a member of the Sanhedrin, or John Mark.
Ἰωάννης.sd: Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four Israelites
Ἰωάννης.as:
Ἰωάννης (D. Ἰωάθας; v. MM, Exp., xᴠ; Bl., § 10, 2), ὁ,
John: Ac 4:613:5, Tr., WH, Re 22:8 (cf. Ἰωάνης).†

Ἰορδάνης.long: the Jordan, a great river flowing due south and bounding Galilee, Samaria, and Judea on the east.
Ἰορδάνης.sd: the Jordanes (i.e. Jarden), a river of Palestine
Ἰορδάνης.as:
Ἰορδάνης, -ου, ὁ (Heb. יַרְדֵּן),
the Jordan: Mt 3:5, Mk 1:5, al.

ἰσχυρός.long: strong (originally and generally of physical strength); mighty, powerful, vehement, sure.
ἰσχυρός.kj: boisterous, mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant
ἰσχυρός.as:
ἰσχυρός, -ά, -όν
(< ἰσχύω), [in LXX for אֵל, גִּבּוֹר, עָצוּם, חָזָק, etc.;]
strong, mighty, powerful;
(a) of persons, as to body or spirit: Mt 12:29, Mk 3:27, Lk 11:21, 22, I Co 4:10 (opp. to ἀσθενής), He 11:34 (ἐν πολέμῳ), Re 5:210:118:2119:18; οἱ πλούσιοι κ. οἱ ἰ., Re 6:15; τὰ ἰ. = οἱ ἰ. (cf. IV Ki 24:15), I Co 1:27; of God (cf. De 10:17), Re 18:8; compar., Mt 3:11, Mk 1:7, Lk 11:22, I Co 1:25 (τὸ ἀσθενὲς τ. θεοῦ) 10:22;
(b) of things: λιμός, Lk 15:14; ἐπιστολαί (βαρεῖαι κ. ἰ.), II Co 10:10; κραυγή, He 5:7; φωνή, Re 18:2; παράκλησις, He 6:18; πόλις, Re 18:10; βρονταί, Re 19:6.†

ἱκανός.long: (a) considerable, sufficient, of number, quantity, time, (b) of persons: sufficiently strong (good, etc.), worthy, suitable, with various constructions, (c) many, much.
ἱκανός.sd: competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character)
ἱκανός.kj: able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy
ἱκανός.der: from ( or , akin to G2240 (ἥκω)) (to arrive);
ἱκανός.as:
ἱκανός, -ή, -όν
(< ἵκω, ἱκάνω, to reach, attain), [in LXX for דַּי, etc.;]
1. of persons, suffcient, competent, fit: c. inf., Mt 3:11, Mk 1:7, Lk 3:16, I Co 15:9, II Co 3:5, II Ti 2:2; seq. πρός, II Co 2:16; seq. ἵνα, Mt 8:8, Lk 7:6.
2. Of things, in number, quantity or size, sufficient, enough, much, many: absol., ἱκανοί, Lk 7:11 (WH, R, omit) 8:32, Ac 12:1214:2119:19, I Co 11:30; ὄχλος ἱ., Mk 10:46, Lk 7:12, Ac 11:24, 2619:26; κλαυθμός, Ac 20:37; ἀργύρια, Mt 28:12; λαμπάδες, Ac 20:8; λόγοι, Lk 23:9; φῶς, Ac 22:6; ἱ, ἐστιν (cf. רַב לָכֶם, LXX ἱκανούσθω, De 3:26), Lk 22:38; τὸ ἱ. ποιεῖν (Lat. satisfacere; cf. Je 31 (48):30), Mk 15:15; τὸ ἱ. λαμβάνειν (Lat. satis accipere; v. M, Pr., 20 f.), Ac 17:9; of time, ἡμέραι ἱ., Ac 9:23, 4318:1827:7; ἱ. χρόνος, Lk 8:27, Ac 8:1114:327:9; pl., Lk 20:9; ἐκ χρόνων ἱ., Lk 23:8; ἀπὸ ἱ. ἐτῶν, Ro 15:23 (WH); ἐφ’ ἱκανόν (cf. II Mac 8:25), Ac 20:11.†

ἱερός.as:
ἱερός, -ά, όν,
[in LXX: Ez 28:18 (מִקְדָּשׁ); τό ἱ., I Ch 29:4 (בַּיִת), Ez 45:19 (עֲזָרָה); very freq. in I Es, I-IV Mac;]
1. in Hom., marvellous, mighty, divine.
2. (Also in Hom. and later cl.) consecrated to the deity, sacred: pl., ἱ. γράμματα, II Ti 3:15.
3. As subst.,
(a) (so in Hom.), τὰ ἱ., sacrifices, sacred rites, sacred things: I Co 9:13;
(b) later, τὸ ἱ., a consecrated or sacred place, a temple: τ. Ἀρτέμιδος, Ac 19:27; of the temple at Jerusalem, i.e. the entire precincts or some part thereof (as distinct from ὁ ναός, q.v., the Sanctuary proper): I Co 9:13, and freq. in Gosp. and esp. in Ac, Mt 12:6, Mk 13:3, Ac 4:1, al. (on the use of ἱ. in Imperial Inser., v. Deiss., LAE, 380 f.)

Ἰάκωβος.long: James, (a) the Small, son of Alphaeus, and one of the Twelve, (b) half-brother of Jesus, (c) father (?) of Jude, (d) son of Zebedee, and brother of John, one of the Twelve, killed A.D. 44.
Ἰάκωβος.sd: Jacobus, the name of three Israelites
Ἰάκωβος.as:
Ἰάκωβος, -ου, ὁ (Heb., v. previous word),
James;
1. Son of Zebedee: Mt 4:21, Mk 1:19, 29, Ac 1:1312:2, al.
2. Son of Alphæus: Mt 10:3, Mk 2:14, al.; commonly identified with Ἰ. ὁ μικρός, James the little, son of Mary (v.s. Μαρία, 3; Κλωπᾶς), Mt 27:56, Mk 15:4016:1 (cf. Jo 19:25).
3. The Lord's brother (v.s. ἀδελφός): Mt 13:55, Mk 6:3, Ac 12:17, al., I Co 15:7 (probably), Ga 1:192:9, 12, Ja 1:1, Ju 1.
4. The father of the apostle, Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου: Lk 6:16, Ac 1:13.

ἰσχύω.long: I have strength, am strong, am in full health and vigor, am able; meton: I prevail.
ἰσχύω.sd: to have (or exercise) force (literally or figuratively)
ἰσχύω.kj: be able, avail, can do(-not), could, be good, might, prevail, be of strength, be whole, + much work
ἰσχύω.as:
ἰσχύω
(< ἰσχύς), [in LXX for חזק, גִּבּוֹר, עצם, etc.;]
1.to be strong in body: Mt 9:12, Mk 2:17.
2.to be powerful, have power, prevail: Ac 19:20, Re 12:8; seq. κατά, c. gen. pers., Ac 19:16; c. inf., to be able (MM, Exp., xv): Mt 8:2826:40, Mk 5:49:18 (inf. understood) 14:37, Lk 6:488:4313:2414:6, 29, 3016:320:26, Jo 21:6, Ac 6:1015:1025:727:16; c. acc., Phl 4:13, Ja 5:16; of things, to avail, be serviceable (MM, Exp., xv): Mt 5:13, Ga 5:6, He 9:17 (cf. ἐν-, ἐξ-, ἐπ-, κατ-ισχύω).†

ἰῶτα.g: a small letter of the Greek alphabet
ἰῶτα.long: iota, a small letter of the Greek alphabet, used in the NT (like yod, the Hebrew or rather Aramaic letter which was the smallest of all) to indicate the smallest part.
ἰῶτα.sd: "iota", the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put (figuratively) for a very small part of anything
ἰῶτα.der: of Hebrew origin (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet);
ἰῶτα.as:
ἰῶτα, τό,
iota (Heb. י, i.e. the smallest letter): Mt 5:18.†

ἱμάτιον.long: a long flowing outer garment, tunic.
ἱμάτιον.kj: apparel, cloke, clothes, garment, raiment, robe, vesture
ἱμάτιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of ennumi (to put on);
ἱμάτιον.as:
ἱμάτιον, -ου, τό
(dim. of εἷμα, a garment), [in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד, also for שִׂמְלָה, שַׂלְמָה, etc.;]
a garment, but in usage always (exc. in p1., v. infr.) of an outer garment, a mantle, cloak (thrown over the χιτών; v. Rutherford, NPhr., 22; DCG, i, 499a): Mt 9:16, 20, 21, Mk 2:215:27, 28, 30, Jo 19:2, Ac 12:8, al.; opp. to χιτών, Mt 5:40, Lk 6:29, Ac 9:39; pl., garments, clothes (i.e. the cloak and the tunic), Mt 17:226:6527:31, 35, Mk 5:3015:20, 24, Jo 19:23, 24, Ja 5:2, al.

ἰχθύς.as:
ἰχθύς, -ύoς, ὁ,
[in LXX for דָּג, דָּגָה;]
a fish: Mt 7:10, Mk 6:38, al.

ἱερεύς.long: a priest, one who offers sacrifice to a god (in Jewish and pagan religions; of Christians only met.).
ἱερεύς.as:
ἱερεύς, -έως, ὁ
(< ἱερός), [in LXX for כָּהֵן;]
a priest: ἱ. τ. Διός, Ac 14:13; of Jewish priests, Mt 8:412:4, 5, Mk 1:442:26, Lk 1:55:14, Jo 1:19, He 8:4, al.; of Christ, He 5:6(LXX)He 10:21; of Christians, Re 1:65:1020:6 (Cremer, 293; on the acc. pl., ἱερεῖς, v. Thack., Gr., 147 f.; Bl., § 8, 2).

ἰάομαι.long: I heal, generally of the physical, sometimes of spiritual, disease.
ἰάομαι.der: middle voice of apparently a primary verb;
ἰάομαι.as:
ἰάομαι, -ῶμαι,
[in LXX for רפא (Ge 20:17, al.), exc. Is 30:2661:1 (חבשׁ);]
to heal: c. acc. pers., Lk 5:176:199:2, 11, 4214:422:51, Jo 4:47, Ac 9:3410:3828:8; pass., Mt 8:8, 1315:28, Lk 7:78:4717:15, Jo 5:13; id. seq. ἀπό, Mk 5:29, Lk 6:17; fig., of spiritual healing, Mt 13:15, Jo 12:40, Ac 28:27(LXX); pass., He 12:13, Ja 5:16, I Pe 2:24.†
SYN.: θεραπεύω, q.v.

ἴδιος.long: one's own, belonging to one, private, personal; one's own people, one's own family, home, property.
ἴδιος.sd: pertaining to self, i.e. one's own; by implication, private or separate
ἴδιος.kj: X his acquaintance, when they were alone, apart, aside, due, his (own, proper, several), home, (her, our, thine, your) own (business), private(-ly), proper, severally, their (own)
ἴδιος.as:
ἴδιος, -α, -ον (in Attic usually -ος, -ον),
[in LXX chiefly for pers. suff., also for לָהֶם, etc.; (τὰ ἴ.) בֵּיתוֹ;]
1.one's own;
(a) of that which is private and personal (in cl. opp. to κοινός, δημόσιος; cf. infr. 3);
(b) of property, friends, home, country, etc. (in cl. opp. to ἀλλότριος; in late writers often, like ἑαυτοῦ, with weakened sense, v. M, Pr., 87 ff.; Deiss., BS, 123 f.): Lk 6:41, Jo 1:425:43, Ac 2:620:28, I Co 11:21, Ga 6:5, II Ti 1:9, He 7:27, Ju 6, al.; πράσσειν τὰ ἴ., I Th 4:11; κατὰ τὰς ἰ. ἐπιθυμίας, II Ti 4:3; οἱ ἴδιοι, Jo 1:11 (M, Pr., 90 f.; Field, Notes, 84) 13:1, Ac 4:23, I Ti 5:8; τὰ ἴδια, one's home (Field, Notes, 84), Lk 18:28, Jo 1:1116:3219:27.
2.peculiar, distinct, appropriate, proper: τὸ ἴ. σῶμα, I Co 15:38; ἐν τ. ἰ. τάγματι, I Co 15:23; εἰς τ. τόπον τ. ἴ., Ac 1:25; = αὐτοῦ (v. Deiss., ut. supr.), Mt 22:5, Jo 1:42 (cf. Wi 10:1).
3. Adverbially (v. supr., 1 (a); and cf. WM, 7392);
(a)ἰδίᾳ, severally, separately: I Co 12:11;
(b)κατ’ ἰδίαν, apart, privately, in private: Mt 14:13, 2320:17, Mk 4:347:33, Lk 10:23, Ac 23:19, al.

ἰατρός.as:
ἰατρός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< ἰάομαι), [in LXX for רֹפֵא;]
a physician: Mt 9:12, Mk 2:175:26, Lk 4:235:318:43 (om. WH, R, mg.), Col 4:14 (on the status of physicians, v. MM, Exp., xv.).†

Ἰσκαριώτης.sd: inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes (i.e. Keriothite), an epithet of Judas the traitor
Ἰσκαριώτης.der: of Hebrew origin (probably H0377 and H07149);
Ἰσκαριώτης.as:
ἰσκαριώθ, ὁ indecl.
(Mk 3:1914:10, Lk 6:16, elsewhere -ιώτης; V. infr.) and Ἰσκαριώτης, -ου (Heb. prob. אִישׁ קְרִיּוֹת; v. Swete, Mk., 3:19),
Iscariot: surname of Judas, Mk 3:1914:10, Lk 6:16 supr., also Mt 10:426:14, Mk 14:43 (WH, R, omit), Lk 22:3, Jo 12:413:214:22; of his father Simon, Jo 6:7113:26.†

Ἰωνᾶς.sd: Jonas (i.e. Jonah), the name of two Israelites
Ἰωνᾶς.as:
Ἰωνᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Heb. יוֹנָה),
Jonah, the prophet: Mt 12:39-4116:4, Lk 11:29, 30, 32.†

ἰχθύδιον.as:
* ἰχθύδιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ἰχθύς),
a little fish: Mt 15:34, Mk 8:7.†

ἵλεως.sd: cheerful (as attractive), i.e. propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in averting some calamity) far be it
ἵλεως.der: perhaps from the alternate form of G138 (αἱρέομαι);
ἵλεως.as:
ἵλεως, -ων
(Att. for ἵλαος), [in LXX for חָלִיל, I Ki 14:45, II Ki 20:20, al.; ἵ. εἶναι, סלח, III Ki 8:30 ff., Je 38(31):34, al.;]
propitious, merciful: τ. ἀδικίαις, He 8:12 (Je 38(31):34; cf. III Ki 8:30 ff.); ἵ. σοι (sc. ἔστω ὁ θεός), Mt 16:22 (cf. I Ki 14:45).†

ἴσος.der: probably from G1492 (εἴδω) (through the idea of seeming);
ἴσος.as:
ἴσος
(epic ἶσος, so sometimes Rec.), -η, -ον, [in LXX for כְּ׳, Jb5:14Jb 10:10, al.; אֶחָד, Ez 40:5 ff.; II Mac 9:15, IV Mac 13:20, 21, al.;]
equal, the same in size, number, quality, etc.: δωρεά, Ac 11:17; μαρτυρίαι, Mk 14:56, 59; ἴ. ποιεῖν, c. acc. et dat., Mt 20:12; ἑαυτὸν τ. θεῷ, Jo 5:18; τὰ ἴ. ἀπολαβεῖν, Lk 6:34, n. pl., ἴσα, adverbially, Re 21:16; τ. θεῷ, Phl 2:6.†

Ἰεριχώ.long: Jericho, a city a little north of the Dead Sea.

Ἰερουσαλήμ.long: (Aramaic form), Jerusalem, the capital of Palestine: hence Judaism, and allegorically, Christendom, the Christian Church.
Ἰερουσαλήμ.sd: Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of Palestine

ἴδε.sd: used as an interjection to denote surprise; lo!
ἴδε.der: second person singular imperative active of G1492 (εἴδω);
ἴδε.as:
ἴδε (Attic ἰδέ; the "later" accentuation is also found in Hom.; Veitch, 215)
1. prop., 2 aor. imperat. of ὁράω, q.v.
2. As interjection, apart from the construction of the sentence, and used where one or many are addressed, see! behold! lo!: Mt 25:20, 22, 25, Mk 2:243:3411:2113:1, 2115:4, 3516:6, Jo 1:29, 36, 483:265:147:2611:3, 3612:1916:2918:2119:4, 14, 26, 27, Ga 5:2.†

Ἱεροσολυμίτης.sd: a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma
Ἱεροσολυμίτης.as:
Ἱεροσολυμεῖτης (WH, Ἰερ-; Rec. -μίτης), -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Si 50:27(29) II Mac 4:22, 39 (V* -μήτης) 18:5*;]
an inhabitant of Jerusalem: Mk 1:5, Jo 7:25.†

ἱμάς.long: a thong, strap, (a) for binding a man who is to be flogged, (b) for fastening a sandal or shoe.
ἱμάς.sd: a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a sandal) or the lash (of a scourge)
ἱμάς.der: perhaps from the same as G260 (ἅμα);
ἱμάς.as:
ἱμάς, -άντος, ὁ,
[in LXX: Is 5:27 (שְׂרוֹךְ), Si 30:35 (33:26), IV Mac 9:11, al;]
a thong, strap: for binding prisoners (IV Mac 9:11, Si 30:35 (33:26)), Ac 22:25; for fastening sandals, Mk 1:7, Lk 3:16, Jo 1:27.†

Ἰδουμαία.long: Idumea, Edom, a district of Arabia, immediately south of Judea.
Ἰδουμαία.sd: Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine
Ἰδουμαία.as:
Ἰδουμαία, -ας, ἡ
(Heb. אֱדוֹם), [in LXX: II Ki 8:14, a1.; elsewhere, as Ge 25:30, Ἐδώμ;]
Idumæa: Mk 3:8.†

Ἰσκαριώθ.sd: inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes (i.e. Keriothite), an epithet of Judas the traitor
Ἰσκαριώθ.der: of Hebrew origin (probably H0377 and H07149);
Ἰσκαριώθ.as:
ἰσκαριώθ, ὁ indecl.
(Mk 3:1914:10, Lk 6:16, elsewhere -ιώτης; V. infr.) and Ἰσκαριώτης, -ου (Heb. prob. אִישׁ קְרִיּוֹת; v. Swete, Mk., 3:19),
Iscariot: surname of Judas, Mk 3:1914:10, Lk 6:16 supr., also Mt 10:426:14, Mk 14:43 (WH, R, omit), Lk 22:3, Jo 12:413:214:22; of his father Simon, Jo 6:7113:26.†

ἱματίζω.long: I clothe, provide clothing for; pass: I am clothed.
ἱματίζω.as:
*† ἱματίζω
(< ἱμάτιον),
to clothe: Mk 5:15, Lk 8:35 (elsewhere only in π.; cf. MM, Exp., xv; Deiss., LAE, 78 f.).†

Ἰάϊρος.long: Jairus, a Jewish ruler of the synagogue.
Ἰάϊρος.as:
Ἰάειρος, -ου, ὁ (Heb. יָאִיר, Nu 32:41),
Jairus: Mk 5:22, Lk 8:41.†

Ἰωσῆς.long: (Hebrew), Joses (a) son of Eliezer, (b) son of Mary, half-brother of Jesus, (c) surnamed Barnabas (also called Joseph).
Ἰωσῆς.sd: Joses, the name of two Israelites
Ἰωσῆς.as:
Ἰωσῆς, -ῆ (Rec. -ή, Lk 3:29; AV, Jose; v.s. Ἰησοῦς, 3), and -ῆτος (Mk 6:315:40, 47), ὁ,
Joses;
1. brother of our Lord: Mk 6:3, Mt 13:55 (Rec., v.s. Ἰωσήφ).
2. Son of Mary: Mt 27:56 (-σήφ, WH, txt), Mk 15:40, 47.
3. v.s. Βαρνάβας.†

ἰσχύς.sd: compare , a form of G2192 (ἔχω)); forcefulness (literally or figuratively)
ἰσχύς.as:
ἰσχύς, -ύος, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for כֹּחַ, also for חַיִל, עֹז, גְּבוּרָה, etc.;]
strength, might, power, force, ability: Re 5:127:12; ἰ. κ. δύναμις, II Pe 2:11; τ. κράτος τῆς ἰ. (Is 40:26), Eph 1:196:10; ἡ δόξα τῆς ἰ., II Th 1:9; ἐξ ἰ., I Pe 4:11; ἐν ὅλῃ τ. ἰ., Mk 12:30, 33(LXX), Lk 10:27(LXX).†
SYN.: δύναμις (q.v., and cf. ICC, Phl 4:13); κράτος (cf. M, Th., I, 1:9).

ἱερατεύω.sd: to be a priest, i.e. perform his functions
ἱερατεύω.as:
ἱερατεύω
(cl. = ἱεράομαι), [in LXX chiefly for כּהן pi.;]
to be a priest, officiate as a priest: Lk 1:8 (the word is freq. in Inscr.; v. LS, s.v.; Deiss., BS, 215; LAE, 70; Cremer, 734).†

ἱερατεία.long: the duty (office) of a priest, priesthood.
ἱερατεία.kj: office of the priesthood, priest's office
ἱερατεία.as:
ἱερατεία (WH, -ία), -ας, ἡ
(< ἱερατεύω), [in LXX for כּהן pi., כְּהֻנָּה (Ex 29:9, al.), exc. Ho 3:4 (אֵפוֹד)*;]
priesthood, office of priest: Lk 1:9, He 7:5.†

Ἰτουραῖος.long: Ituraean, an adjective applied to a district also called Trachonitis, about 60 miles east of the Sea of Galilee, and partly inhabited by the nomad tribe called Ituraeans.
Ἰτουραῖος.sd: Ituræa (i.e. Jetur), a region of Palestine
Ἰτουραῖος.as:
Ἰτουραῖος, -αία, -αῖον,
[in LXX: I Ch 5:19 A (יְטוּר)*;]
Ituræan (in cl. always ὁι Ἰ., the Ituræans) χώρα (ἡ Ἰτουραίων ὀρεινή, τὰ τῶν Ἰ. μέρη, Strabo, XVI, ii, 16, 20), Lk 3:1 (cf. Exp. (1894), ix, 51 ff., 143 ff., 288 ff.).†

Ἰανναί.long: Jannai, an ancestor of Jesus; Jannai was the son of Joseph, and father of Melchi.

Ἰωανάν.as:
Ἰωανάν (Rec. Ἰωαννᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ indecl. (Heb. יוֹחָנָן),
Joanan (cf. Ἰωάνης): Lk 3:37.†

Ἰάρετ.long: (Hebrew), Jared, son of Mahalalel and father of Enoch.
Ἰάρετ.as:
Ἰάρετ (Rec. -ρέδ, L, Ἰάρεθ), ὁ (Heb. יֶרֶד, LXX Ἰάρεδ, FlJ, Ἰάρεδος),
Jared (Ge 5:15): Lk 3:37.†

ἱματισμός.as:
† ἱματισμός, -ού
(< ἱματίζω), [in LXX: Ge 24:53, II Ch 18:29, Ez 16:18, al. (בֶּגֶד); Ex 3:2212:35, Ru 3:3, al. (שִׂמְלָה), etc.;]
clothing, apparel (usually of sumptuous attire; v. Tr., Syn., § 1): Lk 7:259:29, Jo 19:24 (Ps 21:18 (22:19), LXX for לְבוּשׁ), Ac 20:33, I Ti 2:9.†

Ἰωάννα.long: (Hebrew), Joanna, Johanna, wife of Chuza, Herod's steward.
Ἰωάννα.der: feminine of the same as G2491 (Ἰωάννης);
Ἰωάννα.as:
Ἰωάνα (TR, -ννα; v. WH, App., 159), -ης, ἡ (Aram יוֺחַן),
Joanna: Lk 8:324:10.†

ἰκμάς.as:
ἰκμάς, -άδος, ἡ,
[in LXX. Je 17:8 (יוּבַל), Jb 26:14 (שֶׁמֶץ)*;]
moisture: Lk 8:6.†

ἴασις.as:
ἴασις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἰάομαι), [in LXX chiefly for מַרְפֵּא;]
a healing, cure: Ac 4:22, 30; pl., Lk 13:32.†
SYN.: v.s. θεραπεία, 2; ἴαμα, 2.

ἱλάσκομαι.long: (a) I have mercy on, show favor to, (b) trans. with object of sins: I forgive, pardon.
ἱλάσκομαι.sd: to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious
ἱλάσκομαι.der: middle voice from the same as G2436 (ἵλεως);
ἱλάσκομαι.as:
ἱλάσκομαι
(< ἵλαος = ἵλεως), [in LXX (cf. Westc., Epp. Jo., 85 f.) for סלח, IV Ki 5:1824:4, Ps 24(25):11, La 3:42, Da TH 9:19; כּפר pi., Ps 64(65):377(78):3878(79):9; נחם ni., Ex 32:14, Es 4:17*;]
1. in cl., c. acc. pers., to conciliate, appease, propitiate (= ἐξιλάσκομαι, Ge 32:20, Pr 16:14, Ma 1:9, al.).
2. In LXX (Thackeray, Gr., 270, f.), Inscr. (Deiss., BS, 224 f.), and NT, to be propitious, merciful (c. dat. rei, Ps 78(79):9, al.): c. dat. pers. (IV Ki 5:18), Lk 18:13.
3. As in Philo (= ἐξιλάσκ-, in LXX: Ez 43:22, al.), to expiate, make propitiation for: τ. ἁμαρτίας, He 2:17 (Cremer, 301 ff., 735).†

ἴσως.long: perhaps, equally; it may be that.
ἴσως.as:
ἴσως
(< ἴσσς),
adv.,
[in LXX for אוּלַי, אַךְ, הֵן, Ge 32:20, Je 5:4, al.;]
1.equally.
2.perhaps: Lk 20:13.†

ἰσάγγελος.long: equal to or like the angels.
ἰσάγγελος.as:
*† ἰσάγγελος, -ον
(< ἴσος, ἄγγελος),
like or equal to angels: Lk 20:36.†

ἱδρώς.der: a strengthened form of a primary idos (sweat);
ἱδρώς.as:
ἱδρώς
(Tr. -ῶς), -ῶτος, ὁ, [in LXX: Ge 3:19 (זֵעָה), II Mac 2:26, IV Mac 7:8*;]
sweat: Lk 22:44 (WH, omit).†

Ἰσραηλίτης.long: an Israelite, one of the chosen people of Israel, a Jew.
Ἰσραηλίτης.sd: an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or figuratively)
Ἰσραηλίτης.as:
Ἰσραηλείτης
(Rec. -λίτης),ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Nu 25:8 (יִשְׂרָאֵל), III Ki 20 (21):1 (יִזְרְעֵאלִי; Luc. Ἰεζραηλίτης), etc.;]
an Israelite, the name expressive of theocratic privilege (v.s. Ἑβραῖος): Ro 9:411:1, II Co 11:22; ἀληθῶς Ἰ., Jo 1:48; ἄνδρες Ἰ., Ac 2:223:125:3513:1621:28.†

Ἰοῦστος.long: Justus, (a) a surname of Joseph Barsabbas, one of the two nominated to fill Judas' place as apostle, (b) Titius Justus, a Corinthian Christian, (c) surname of Jesus, a Christian with Paul in Rome.
Ἰοῦστος.sd: Justus, the name of three Christian
Ἰοῦστος.as:
Ἰοῦστος, -ου, ὁ,
Justus, the surname of,
1.Joseph Barsabbas: Ac 1:23.
2.Titus, of Corinth: Ac 18:7.
3.Jesus, a Christian of Rome: Col 4:11.†

ἰδιώτης.long: (unofficial, hence) an amateur, an unprofessional man, a layman; an ungifted person.
ἰδιώτης.sd: a private person, i.e. (by implication) an ignoramus (compare "idiot")
ἰδιώτης.as:
ἰδιώτης, -ου, ὁ
(< ἴδιος), [in LXX: Pr 6:8 (no Heb.)*;]
1.a private person, as opp. to the State or an official (βασιλεῖς κ. ἰδιῶται, Pr 6:8; and cf. MM, Exp., xv).
2.one without professional knowledge, unskilled, uneducated, unlearned: I Co 14:16, 23, 24 (R, mg., without gifts); ἀγράμματοι κ. ἰ., Ac 4:13; c. dat. (= cl. c. gen. rei), λόγῳ, II Co 11:6.†

Ἰόππη.long: Joppa, a coast town of Judea, west-north-west of Jerusalem.
Ἰόππη.sd: Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in Palestine
Ἰόππη.as:
Ἰόππη (FlJ, id., and also Ἰόπη), -ης, ἡ, (Heb. יָפוֹ),
Joppa: Ac 91011.†

Ἰκόνιον.long: Iconium, a Phrygian city of the Roman province Galatia (modern Konia).
Ἰκόνιον.sd: image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia Minor
Ἰκόνιον.as:
Ἰκόνιον, -ου, τό,
Iconium, a city of the province of Galatia: Ac 13:5114:1, 19, 2116:2, II Ti 3:11.†

Ἰάσων.long: Jason, a Christian of Thessalonica, perhaps the same as the "relative" of Paul.
Ἰάσων.sd: about to cure; Jason, a Christian
Ἰάσων.der: future active participle masculine of G2390 (ἰάομαι);
Ἰάσων.as:
Ἰάσων, -ονος, ὁ,
Jason: Ac 17:5-7, 9; perhaps the same, Ro 16:21.†

Ἰταλία.as:
Ἰταλία, -ας, ἡ,
Italy: ἡ Ἰ. (v. Bl., § 46, 11), Ac 18:227:1, 6, He 13:14.†

ἱερόσυλος.long: robbing temples, but possibly simply: sacrilegious.
ἱερόσυλος.as:
** ἱερόσυλος, -ον
(< ἱερόν, συλάω), [in LXX: II Mac 4:42 (cf. -λημα, II Mac 4:39; -λία, 13:6)*;]
robbing temples: Ac 19:37.†

ἱππεύς.long: a horse-soldier, a mounted soldier, a cavalryman.
ἱππεύς.sd: an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps
ἱππεύς.as:
ἱππεύς, -έως (on acc. pl., -εῖς, ν. Bl., § 8, 2; Thack., Gr., 148),ὁ
(< ἵππος), [in LXX chiefly for פָּרָשׁ;]
a horseman: Ac 23:23, 32.†

Ἰούλιος.long: Julius, a Roman centurion on special service.

ἱεροσυλέω.long: I commit sacrilege, rob a temple.
ἱεροσυλέω.as:
** ἱερο-συλέω, -ῶ
(< ἱερόσυλος, q.v.), [in LXX: II Mac 9:2*;]
to rob a temple (commit sacrilege, R, mg.): Ro 2:22.†

ἰός.sd: rust (as if emitted by metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents)
ἰός.as:
ἰός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX: Ez 24:6, 11, 12 (חֶלְאָה), Ps 139 (140):3 (חֵמָה), al.;]
1.an arrow.
2.rust (Ez 24:6): Ja 5:3 (cf. MM, Exp., xv).
3.poison: fig., Ro 3:13(Ps 139 (140):3), Ja 3:8.†

ἱλαστήριον.long: (a) a sin offering, by which the wrath of the deity shall be appeased; a means of propitiation, (b) the covering of the ark, which was sprinkled with the atoning blood on the Day of Atonement.
ἱλαστήριον.sd: an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple)
ἱλαστήριον.der: neuter of a derivative of G2433 (ἱλάσκομαι);
ἱλαστήριον.as:
† ἱλαστήριος, -α, -ον
(< ἱλάσκομαι), [in LXX: IV Mac 17:22; neut., Ex 25:16(17) ff. 31:735:1238:5 (37:6) ff., Le 16:2, 13 ff. Nu 7:89 (כַּפֹּרֶת), Ez 43:14, 17, 20 (עֲזָרָה) Am 9:1 (on the original here, v. Deiss., BS, 127)*;]
propitiatory (μνῆμα, FlJ, Ant., xvi, 7, 1; θάνατος, II Mac, l.c.): of Christ, Ro 3:25; as subst., το ἱ. (sc. ἐπίθεμα, Ex 25:16, 17, where the word first occurs in LXX and where ἱ. ἐ. = כַּפֹּרֶת (q.v. in BDB, s.v.), elsewhere rendered simply τὸ ἱ; cf. Deiss., 124 ff.; Westc., He., in l.), He 9:5.†

ἴχνος.as:
ἴχνος, -εος (-ους), τό,
[in LXX for כַּף, etc.;]
a track, footstep: metaph. (as freq. in cl.), στοιχεῖν τοῖς ἴ., Ro 4:12; περιπατεῖν τοῖς ἴ., II Co 12:18; ἐπακολουθεῖν τοῖς ἴ., I Pe 2:21 (cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

ἱλαρότης.as:
† ἱλαρότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< ἱλαρός), [in LXX: Pr 18:22 (רָצוֹן)*;]
cheerfulness: Ro 12:8.†

ἱερουργέω.sd: to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively)
ἱερουργέω.der: from a compound of G2411 (ἱερόν) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον);
ἱερουργέω.as:
**† ἱερουργέω, -ῶ
(< ἱερουργός, a sacrificing priest) [in LXX: IV Mac 7:3 R (cf. -γία, IV Mac 3:30א R)*;]
to perform sacred rites; c. acc., to minister in priestly service (minister in sacrifice, R, mg.), τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, Ro 15:16.†

Ἰλλυρικόν.long: Illyricum, a Roman province, afterwards called Dalmatia, bounded by Pannonia on the north, Macedonia on the south, Moesia on the east, and the Adriatic Sea on the west.
Ἰλλυρικόν.sd: (the) Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of Europe
Ἰλλυρικόν.der: neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation;
Ἰλλυρικόν.as:
Ἰλλυρικόν, -οῦ, τό,
Illyricum, a region bordering on the Adriatic Sea: Ro 15:19.†

Ἰουλία.long: Julia, a Roman Christian, probably a slave or freed from the Imperial household.
Ἰουλία.der: feminine of the same as G2457 (Ἰούλιος);

ἱερόθυτος.as:
* ἱερόθυτος, -ον (< ἱερός, θύω),
offered in sacrifice: I Co 10:28 (Rec. εἰδωλοθ-).†

ἴαμα.as:
ἴαμα, -τος, τό
(< ἰάομαι), [in LXX for מַרְפֵּא (II Ch 36:16, Ec 10:4, Je 40 (33):6), etc.;]
1. most freq. in cl., a means of healing, remedy (Thuc., al.; Wi 11:410:9).
2. = ἴασις (q.v.), a healing (Plat.; Je 40 (33):6): pl., I Co 12:9, 28, 30.†

ἱκανόω.long: I make sufficient, render fit, qualify.
ἱκανόω.as:
† ἱκανόω, -ῶ
(< ἱκανός), [in LXX chiefly for רַב;]
to make sufficient, render fit: c. dupl. acc., II Co 3:6; c. acc. pers. seq. εἰς, Col 1:12.†

ἰσότης.sd: likeness (in condition or proportion); by implication, equity
ἰσότης.as:
ἰσότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< ἴσος), [in LXX: Jb 36:30, Za 4:7*;]
1.equality: II Co 8:13, 14.
2.equity, fairness: τὸ δίκαιον κ. τὴν ἰ., Col 4:1 (for distinction bet. τὸ δ. and ἡ ἰ., v. ICC, in l).†

ἱλαρός.sd: propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing
ἱλαρός.as:
ἱλαρός, -ά, -όν
(< ἵλαος = ἵλεως, q.v.), [in LXX: Pr 19:12 (רָצוֹן) 22:8, Es 5:1, Jb 33:26, Si 13:2626:4, III Mac 6:35*;]
cheerful, joyous: II Co 9:7 (Pr 22:8(9)(LXX)).†

Ἰουδαϊσμός.sd: "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages
Ἰουδαϊσμός.as:
† Ἰουδαϊσμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< Ἰουδαΐζω), [in LXX: II Mac 2:218:114:38, IV Mac 4:26*;]
Judaism, the observance of Jewish rites: Ga 1:13, 14.†

ἱστορέω.sd: to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview)
ἱστορέω.as:
** ἱστορέω, -ῶ
(< ἵστωρ, one learned or skilled in) [in LXX: I Es 1:33, 42*;]
1. c. acc. rei, to inquire into, learn by inquiry.
2. C. acc. pers., to inquire of or about.
3.to narrate, record.
4. In late writers, to visit, become acquainted with: Ga 1:18 (v. Ellic., in l., and cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

Ἰουδαϊκῶς.long: in the manner of Jews (religiously, ceremonially).
Ἰουδαϊκῶς.sd: Judaïcally or in a manner resembling a Judæan

ἰουδαΐζω.long: I live as a Jew (in religion, ceremonially).
ἰουδαΐζω.as:
† Ἰουδαΐζω
(< Ἰουδαῖος), [in LXX: Es 8:17 (יהד hith.)*;]
to conform to Jewish practice, to Judaize: Ga 2:14.†

ἰσόψυχος.long: like-minded, of the same mind or spirit.
ἰσόψυχος.as:
ἰσόψυχος-ον
(< ἴσος, ψυχή), [in LXX: Ps 54(55):13 (כְּעֶרְכִּי)*;]
1.of equal spirit (Æsch., Agam., 1470).
2.like-minded: Phl 2:20.†

Ἱεράπολις.long: Hierapolis, a city of the Lycus valley in Phrygia, near Laodicea and Colossae.
Ἱεράπολις.sd: holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia Minor
Ἱεράπολις.as:
Ἱεράπολις (WH, Ἱερὰ Πόλις), -εως, ἡ,
Hierapolis: a city in the Lycus valley in the Province of Asia: Col 4:13.†

Ἰάννης.long: Jannes, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh.

Ἰαμβρῆς.long: Jambres, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh.

Ἰουδαϊκός.as:
† Ἰουδαϊκός, ή, -όν,
[in LXX: II Mac 8:11 V, 13:21*;]
Jewish: Tit 1:14.†

ἱεροπρεπής.g: suitable to a sacred character, reverent
ἱεροπρεπής.long: suitable to a sacred character, reverent.
ἱεροπρεπής.der: from G2413 (ἱερός) and the same as G4241 (πρέπω);
ἱεροπρεπής.as:
** ἱεροπρεπής, -ές
(< ἱερός, πρέπει), [in LXX: IV Mac 9:2511:20*;]
suited to a sacred character, reverend (RV, reverent): Tit 2:3 (cf. Tr., Syn., § xcii).†

ἱκετηρία.long: (originally: the olive branch held in the hand of the suppliant), supplication, entreaty.
ἱκετηρία.der: from a derivative of the base of G2425 (ἱκανός) (through the idea of approaching for a favor);
ἱκετηρία.as:
ἱκετήριος, -α, -ον
(< ἱκέτης, a suppliant), [in LXX: Jb 40:22(27), II Mac 9:18*;]
of a suppliant; as subst., ἡ ἱ. (sc. ῥάβδος),
1. in cl., an olive-branch, carried by a suppliant.
2. In late Gk. = ἱκεσία, supplication: pl., δεήσεις κ. ἱ., He 5:7.
SYN.: v.s. δέησις.

ἱερωσύνη.long: the abstract notion of the priestly office.
ἱερωσύνη.sd: sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office
ἱερωσύνη.as:
ἱερωσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(< ἱερός), [in LXX: I Ch 29:22 (כּהן), I Es 5:38, Si 45:24, I Mac 2:543:497:9, 21, IV Mac 5:357:6*;]
priesthood: He 7:11, 12, 24.†

Ἰεφθάε.long: (Hebrew), Jephthah, one of the Judges of Israel.

ἵππος.as:
ἵππος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for סוּס, sometimes for פָּרָשׁ, רֶכֶב;]
a horse: Ja 3:3, Re 6:2 ff. Re 9:7 ff. Re 14:2018:1319:11 ff.†

Ἰώβ.long: (Hebrew), Job, the hero of the book of that name in the Old Testament.

ἱεράτευμα.g: the act or office of priesthood
ἱεράτευμα.long: the act or office of priesthood.
ἱεράτευμα.sd: the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order (figuratively)
ἱεράτευμα.as:
† ἱεράτευμα, -τος, τό
(< ἱερατεύω), [in LXX: βασίλειον ἱ., Ex 19:6 (כֹּהֲנִיםמַמְלֶכֶת) 23:22, II Mac 2:17*;]
a priesthood, body of priests: ἱ ἅγιον, I Pe 2:5; βασ. ἱ, I Pe 2:9 (LXX, Ex 19:6).†

ἰσότιμος.as:
*† ἰσότιμος, -ον,
(< ἴσος, τιμή),
equally privileged, held in equal honour: πίστις, II Pe 1:1 (R, mg., equally precious, but v Field, Notes, 240; Mayor, in l.).†

ἱλασμός.long: a propitiation (of an angry god), atoning sacrifice.
ἱλασμός.as:
† ἱλασμός, -οῦ
(< ἱλάσκομαι), [in LXX: Le 25:9, Nu 5:8 (כִּפֻּרִים), Ps 129(130):4, Da TH 9:9 (סְלִיחָה), Am 8:14 (אַשְׁמָה), Ez 44:27 (חַטָּאת), I Ch 28:20, Si 18:20 A, II Mac 3:33*;]
1.an appeasing (Plut.).
2.a means of appeasing, propitiation (Philo; Nu 5:8, Ez 44:27): I Jo 2:24:10.
3. In LXX also forgiveness (Ps 129(130):4, Da TH 9:9).†

Ἰεζάβελ.long: Jezebel, name given to a false prophetess of Thyatira, possibly borrowed from the name of Ahab's wife, queen of Israel.
Ἰεζάβελ.sd: Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher)
Ἰεζάβελ.as:
Ἰεζάβελ (L, Ἰεζ-; Tr. -βέλ; Rec. -βήλ) ἡ, indecl. (Heb. אִיזֶבֶל; LXX as txt.; FlJ, Ἰεζαβέλη),
Jezebel (III Ki 16:31, al.): symbolically, Re 2:20 (v. Swete, in l.).†

ἴασπις.as:
ἴασπις, -ιδος, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ex 28:1836:18 (39:11) (יַהֲלֹם), Is 54:12 (כַּדְכֹּד), Ez 28:13 (יָשְׁפֵה, v. BDB, Lex., s.v.)*;]
jasper, apparently not the modern stone of that name, but a translucent stone (DB, s.v.): Re 4:321:11, 18, 19.†

ἶρις.der: perhaps from G2046 (ἐρέω) (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan deities);
ἶρις.as:
ἶρις, -ιδος, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ex 30:24 (קִדָּה)*, (קֶשֶׁת, Ge 9:13, Ez 1:28, is rendered by τόξον);]
1.Iris, the messenger of the gods.
2.a rainbow or halo: Re 4:310:1.
3. The plant Iris (cf. Ex 30:24).†

Ἰσσαχάρ.sd: Isachar (i.e. Jissaskar), a son of Jacob (figuratively, his descendant)
Ἰσσαχάρ.as:
Ἰσσαχάρ (Rec. Ἰσαχ-, Ἰσασχ- (Elz.), T, -άχαρ), ὁ indecl. (FlJ, Ἰσάχαρις, Ἰσάσχ-) (Heb. יִשְׁשָׂכָר, Ge 30:18),
Issachar: Re 7:7.†

ἱππικόν.der: neuter of a derivative of G2462 (ἵππος);
ἱππικόν.as:
** ἱππικός, -ή, -όν
(< ἵππος), [in LXX: I Mac 15:33, III Mac 1:1*;]
of a horse or of horsemen, equestrian; as subst., τὸ ἱ. (sc. στράτευμα), cavalry: He 9:16.†
